stemMd: Carbon dioxide has polar carbon–oxygen bonds but no permanent molecular dipole. What explains this?

options.label: A
options.textMd: A molecule with polar bonds must always have a net dipole.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Oxygen and carbon have identical electronegativity.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Its linear symmetric geometry causes the bond dipoles to cancel.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Carbon dioxide is made only of ions.

explanationMd: Bond polarity and molecular polarity are different. In linear carbon dioxide, equal dipoles point in opposite directions and their vector sum is zero.

distractorRationale.e: The molecular species has covalent bonds.
distractorRationale.a: Molecular geometry can cancel bond dipoles.
